content: Metro West Ambulance operates throughout the state of Oregon, providing ambulance services across Washington County and along the Oregon Coast under the names Pacific West and Medix. Additionally, Metro West manages the Vernonia Volunteer Ambulance Association. Beyond daily emergency ambulance services, Metro West offers a comprehensive wheelchair van service and provides medical support for special events, including Portland's Rose Garden Arena, the Oregon State Fair, and various other events throughout the year. The organization also delivers community medical and preparedness training through its Education for Life program in collaboration with the American Heart Association. Metro West Ambulance is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Ambulance Services. The organization has received several honors, including the Oregon DHS Commitment to Quality Medal in 2002 and 2004, as well as the Oregon DHS EMS Unit Citation awarded to Medix Ambulance in 2006. In 1996, Metro West Ambulance competed for the Washington County medical transport contract. By 1997, the company secured the Washington County, Oregon contract for 9-1-1 dispatch services. However, in 2006, Clackamas County, Oregon, awarded a no-bid contract to Metro West's competitor, AMR, despite objections. Metro West was not present during the final discussions regarding this decision. In 2007, unionized medics from various area ambulance companies approved a strike, citing dissatisfaction with pay and benefits, and comparisons were drawn between their companies and Metro West. In legal matters, Metro West Ambulance successfully defended itself in 2004 against a wrongful termination lawsuit filed by a former employee. However, in 2007, the company was fined by the FCC for transmitting on licensed frequencies with an expired license.
